results.answer:
The AMF (Access and Mobility Management Function) has several roles in the 5G Core network, including:

- Providing the 5G - AN node with weight factors for each TNL association of the AMF [1].
- Requesting the 5G - AN node to add or remove TNL associations to the AMF [1].
- Indicating to the 5G - AN node the set of TNL associations used for UE-associated signalling and the set of TNL associations used for non-UE associated signalling [1].
- Advertising the same AMF Pointer and/or distinct AMF Pointer value(s) to the 5G - AN node [3, 4].
- Publishing information about the AMF in the DNS system to support legacy EPC core network entity (i.e. MME) discovery and communication [3, 4].
- Partitioning GUMMEI and GUAMI encoding space to avoid overlapping values and enable MME discovery of an AMF without ambiguity [3, 4].
- Providing the 5G System architecture with the capability to support multiple TNL associations per AMF [6].
- Indicating to the 5G - AN node the set of TNL associations used for UE-associated signalling and the set of TNL associations used for non-UE associated signalling [6].
- Supporting the legacy EPC core network entity (i.e. MME) to discover and communicate with the AMF [7].
- Maintaining support for emergency services and for MPS during an overload situation [2].
- Recovering and either allowing the possibility of AMFs within the AMF Set to advertise the same AMF Pointer and/or distinct AMF Pointer value(s) to the 5G - AN node or partitioning GUMMEI and GUAMI encoding space to avoid overlapping values [2, 7].

The AMF is also a Network Function in the 5G System architecture, as defined in TS 23.501, 4.2.2 [5].

results.answer:
The 5G Core Network supports two possible deployment scenarios for a PDU Session in the case of roaming: "Local Break Out" (LBO) and "Home Routed" (HR) [8]. 

In the "Local Break Out" (LBO) scenario, the SMF and all UPF(s) involved by the PDU Session are under control of the VPLMN [8].

In the "Home Routed" (HR) scenario, the PDU Session is supported by a SMF function under control of the HPLMN, by a SMF function under control of the VPLMN, by at least one UPF under control of the HPLMN and by at least one UPF under control of the VPLMN [8].
